title: The Shaft That Reached 50.9 MPa, Not 25.5
featured_title: THE SHAFT THAT REACHED 50.9 MPA NOT 25.5
subject: civil

presentation.challenge: The polar moment was correct, but shear stress was evaluated at half the outer radius. Maximum torsional stress occurs at the outside surface and was 50.9 MPa.

practice.primary_question: How is maximum torsional shear stress calculated in a solid circular shaft?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Evaluating τ=Tr/J at an interior radius rather than at the outside radius where maximum shear occurs.

case_dna.target_misconception: Maximum torsional shear stress can be evaluated at r=d/4.
case_dna.why_plausible: Shear stress varies linearly with radius, and an interior radius may be mistaken for a representative location.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For T=1.25 kN·m and d=50 mm, τmax=16T/(πd³)=50.93 MPa at r=d/2.
case_dna.corrected_model: In a solid circular shaft, τ=Tr/J and the maximum occurs at the outer radius c=d/2.

problem_statement: A solid circular steel shaft has diameter d=50 mm and transmits torque T=1.25 kN·m. Determine maximum torsional shear stress. A note evaluates stress at r=12.5 mm instead of the 25 mm outer radius and reports about 25.5 MPa.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The stress equation was evaluated at the wrong radius.
gates.prompt: Where does maximum torsional shear occur?

options.label: τmax=T(d/2)/J=16T/(πd³)
options.reason: Torsional shear stress increases linearly with radius and peaks at the surface.

options.label: Use r=d/4 for maximum stress
options.reason: That gives only half the true maximum stress.

options.label: τ=T/A
options.reason: Torque requires the polar moment relation, not direct division by area.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Move from shaft center to outer surface
gates.result: Maximum torsional shear stress is about 50.9 MPa.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the maximum stress
gates.hint: Use torque in N·mm and diameter in mm.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Torsional shear rises linearly with radius

cards.text: At r=12.5 mm, stress is half as large, about 25.46 MPa.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the shaft-stress note
report: C3. Using r=12.5 mm gives the maximum shear stress, about 25.5 MPa.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Maximum stress occurs at r=25 mm, not 12.5 mm.

evidence_choices.label: τmax=T(25)/J≈50.93 MPa
evidence_choices.reason: This evaluates shear at the outer surface.

correction.template: The maximum torsional shear stress is {tau_max_mpa} MPa.

options.label: Use diameter at least about 54.2 mm

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply torsion again
gates.prompt: A solid shaft has T=0.80 kN·m and d=40 mm. What is τmax?

options.label: About 31.8 MPa
options.reason: That corresponds to evaluating stress at half the outer radius.

gates.explanation: Maximum torsional shear is evaluated at the outside surface.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the torsion calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that maximum torsional shear stress in a solid circular shaft occurs at the outer radius.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The stress was evaluated at an interior radius.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Torsional shear increases linearly from the center to the surface.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use τmax=16T/(πd³) for a solid circular shaft.
